messages.content: 在壓力為10千帕的情況下，水的凝固點是多少？

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point
function.description: Calculate the boiling point of a given substance at a specific pressure. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

substance.description: The substance for which to calculate the boiling point.

pressure.description: The pressure at which to calculate the boiling point. This is a float type value.

unit.description: The unit of the pressure. Default is 'kPa'.

message.content:
**Answer**

At a pressure of **10 kPa** (≈ 0.1 atm) the freezing (melting) point of pure water is only slightly below the standard 0 °C.  
Using the known slope of the ice–water phase boundary (≈ +0.002 K · Pa⁻¹ for the melting curve near 0 °C), the temperature shift from 101.3 kPa down to 10 kPa is:

\[
\Delta T \approx \frac{dT}{dP}\,\Delta P
          \approx 0.002\,\text{K · Pa}^{-1}\times(-91\,300\,\text{Pa})
          \approx -0.18\,\text{K}
\]

So the freezing point at 10 kPa is roughly:

\[
T_{\text{freeze}} \approx 0\,^\circ\text{C} - 0.18\,^\circ\text{C}
                    \approx -0.2\,^\circ\text{C}
\]

**Thus, the freezing point of water at 10 kPa is about –0.2 °C.**

---

### Why I didn’t call the tool

The available `thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point` function only computes boiling points; it does not provide freezing/melting temperatures. Therefore, I used the known phase‑boundary data for ice–water instead of invoking the tool.
